newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q3 EPS expected up - analysts.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q3 EPS expected up - analysts.

text.p: General Mills Inc is projected to report stronger fiscal third quarter earnings on Wednesday, even if its core cereal volume declines as expected, analysts said Tuesday.
"I think you're going to see a flat-ish top line in sales, but better...growth in earnings per share," Sanford Bernstein analyst Steven Galbraith said.
According to First Call, the mean analyst estimate for the third quarter ended in February is $0.78 a share, which compares with $0.73 earned a year ago.

Galbraith said General Mills' third quarter cereal sales volume -- minus any benefit from the recent acquisition of Ralcorp Holdings Inc's branded cereal -- likely would decline compared with a year ago.
That decline, in part, reflects reductions in promotions, which is expected to help the company's bottom line.

Schroder Wertheim analyst Robert Cummins added that General Mills also faces some tough comparisons with the year-ago third quarter when its domestic unit volume was up seven percent and ready-to-eat cereal was up five percent.
In an interview in February, General Mills Chairman Stephen Sanger said he expected modest volume growth in the second half of the fiscal year, but stronger earnings.
In the first half of the year, earnings were relatively flat, partly because of a reduction in cereal prices, while sales benefitted from promotions.
